newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas lifted again by SW heat, futures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas lifted again by SW heat, futures.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices edged higher Wednesday amid a continuing hot spell in the Southwest and an early uptick in the futures market, industry sources said.

"I think it was up early in response to the screen yesterday and a little today, but then it came off at the end," one trader said, referring to Tuesday's August Henry Hub futures rally on NYMEX to a high of $2.142.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices were quoted about three cents higher at $2.14-2.17 per mmBtu at the Henry Hub, as temperatures still hovered in the 90s F across the area.
Following the early climb on NYMEX, August gas futures quickly slipped to a low of $2.08, off 3.6 cents from Tuesday's settlement.
With temperatures still topping 100 degrees in Arizona, Permian prices gained an average of four cents to about $2.05, while southern California border prices rose an equal amount to the mid-$2.20s.
Also boosting prices was news from Arizona Public Service that the 750 megawatt (MW) Four Corners coal-fired power unit in New Mexico would shut Friday for three weeks for repairs.
Also, the 1,080 MW San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in California was expected to remain off line until late next week.
The adjacent unit 3, with a generating capacity of 1,080 MW, was slated to restart Saturday, according to the company.

Preventing a sharper uptick in western prices, traders said, were moderate weather patterns in southern California. According to Weather Services Corp, temperature highs are forecast to remain in the low-80s F over the next few days.
In the East, swing prices at the New York city-gate held in the high-$2.30s as moderate weather in the region continued to keep a lid on cooling demand.
In the Midwest, swing prices rose about three cents to $2.02-2.04. Chicago city-gate prices were quoted equally higher at $2.19-2.20.
Separately, Transco reported earlier today that it restored the 400 million cubic feet per day of gas shut in late Tuesday after a leak was detected on a small offshore Louisiana line.
According to a Reuter poll, most traders are expecting a injection rate of 83-88 bcf in today's American Gas Association storage report. A year ago 90 bcf of gas was injected into storage.
